key_insight: A context-aware Markov decision process can personalize Type 2 diabetes follow-up timing, replacing one-size-fits-all visit intervals with risk-stratified recommendations.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help primary care teams schedule follow-ups more efficiently by matching visit frequency to patient risk and recent clinical status.
method: Used EHR data from 22,154 adults with Type 2 diabetes across 10 primary care clinics.
Created patient contexts with PCA-based trajectory features plus clustering and additional patient-level variables.
Learned context-specific follow-up interval policies with a contextual Markov decision process.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, the CMDP policy lowered expected cumulative cost versus a fixed-interval comparator, including about 34.8% reduction in the higher-comorbidity context and 6.4% in the lower-comorbidity context.
watch_item: The model was derived from retrospective EHR data, so real-world deployment would need validation for safety, fairness, and workflow fit before use.
paper_title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes
